result.summary:
Read docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-038.md in full independently (both proposed files' complete source, not the AC-to-case map alone). Read GitHub issue #70 directly for the exact wording of all 11 ACs. Read docs/agents/design/REQ-038.md in full. Read the actual implementation: apps/bot/src/domain/inviteCode.ts's redeemInviteCode (lines 616-826), validateInviteCodeForRedemption (557-594), getInviteCodeByCode/normalizeInviteCode (510-538), parseRedeemArgs; apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts's hasPastCheckIn (132-139), decideRegistrationOutcome's inviteSatisfied gate (34-93), registerForEvent's new internal step (206-218); apps/bot/src/handlers/registration.ts's makeRedeemCommandHandler; apps/bot/src/handlers/start.ts's resolveInviteDeepLink/i_ dispatch/makeConsentCallbackHandler's invite branch. Every function/type/signature the spec's test source calls was confirmed to exist verbatim in the real committed code -- no invented API.

No TODO in the spec. All 11 ACs have at least one precise, mechanically-followable verification case (exact function calls, exact expected outcome.kind values, exact row/field assertions) -- verified the AC-to-case map against issue #70's literal AC text one by one and confirmed each case's assertions actually match what the AC requires (e.g. AC2's case checks BOTH zero registration for B AND unchanged used_count, plus a positive control that A's own redemption succeeds; AC3's four sub-cases are genuinely distinct constructed scenarios -- expired via PAST_EXPIRY, spent via usedCount forced to maxUses, unknown via a literal nonexistent code string, wrong-event via a second seeded event passed as explicitEventId -- each independently asserting zero registrations and unchanged used_count; AC7 has both the positive (checked_in_at set directly, then registerForEvent admits with zero code involvement) and negative (no check-in, registerForEvent refuses 'requires-invite') cases plus a static grep of schema.ts for is_?returning|returning_status|attended_before|past_attendee|eligib -- confirmed by an independent grep that no such column exists on this branch, so the check would genuinely catch a real violation; AC9 exercises a redeemer with zero prior consent, confirms zero profiles rows and no registration both immediately after the prompt and after an unrelated follow-up /start with no consent:agree tap -- independently confirmed via grep that this codebase's consent flow (domain/consent.ts, handlers/start.ts) has no separate 'decline' affordance, only consent:agree, so the spec's framing of 'declining' as 'never taps agree' is accurate, not a cop-out).

tg_id ranges independently re-verified via `grep -rn "let nextTgId|let tgSeq" apps/bot/src`: highest pre-existing band is 1_040_000_000 (handlers/inviteCodes.db.test.ts). The spec's claimed 1_050_000_000+ and 1_051_000_000+ are both comfortably above every existing band -- confirmed collision-free.

AC4 concurrency test (the highest-stakes check) verified in full detail against both proposed cases: (1) Genuinely concurrent -- both redeemInviteCode(...) calls are invoked directly inside the Promise.all(...) argument array (never awaited individually first), matching the exact anti-serialization pattern registrationApproval.db.test.ts's own already-validated REQ-035 AC5 case uses. The higher-fan-in case uses a dedicated `new Pool({ max: 30 })`, fires all 10 calls via .map(...) into Promise.all, and asserts `highConcurrencyPool.totalCount` immediately after firing (via a setImmediate tick) but before any call has necessarily completed -- byte-for-byte the same evidence-of-genuine-parallelism assertion shape (`toBeGreaterThan(Math.min(1, totalCountBefore))` and `toBeGreaterThan(1)`) as registrationApproval.db.test.ts lines 237/247-248 for REQ-035's own AC5, confirmed by direct comparison. (2) Isolation from capacity: every seeded event across both AC4 cases uses capacity 50 while the fan-in never exceeds 10 -- capacity is never the bottleneck, so a capacity-driven waitlist outcome cannot produce 'exactly one success' by accident; only the invite_codes row's own FOR UPDATE lock (confirmed at inviteCode.ts lines 662-673, taken fresh inside the transaction, never reusing the unlocked step-2 precheck at line 627) can produce the observed exactly-one-winner result. (3) The invariant traced precisely: literal case seeds maxUses=2 with usedCount forced to 1 (one use left), asserts post-race usedCount===2 (== maxUses, never above) and exactly 1 admitted registration row; higher-fan-in case seeds maxUses=FAN_IN(10) with usedCount forced to FAN_IN-1, asserts post-race usedCount===FAN_IN and exactly 1 admitted row, with admittedCount===1 and spentCount===FAN_IN-1 read directly off the returned outcomes. Both match AC4's literal text ('exactly one successful registration and used_count ending at max_uses, never above it') and the requirement's 'repeated at least 20 times' (literal case runs exactly 20 iterations).

AC8's design-artefact string-match case was independently checked against the actual design doc text: docs/agents/design/REQ-038.md section 8 contains 'This design takes resolution (a): the rule applies uniformly to every `requires_invite` event' (matches the spec's expected substring 'resolution (a): the rule applies uniformly to every') and 'No column is added to `events`, `users`, or any other table by this design' (matches 'No column is added to `events`'). Both substrings are present verbatim in the current file.

No issues found. No rework required.
